surviving_research.question: Can a cheap exact-state feature predict cross-worker critical-path leverage well enough to outperform rank-neutral hash thinning?

negative_results: Shared-hit local backfill reduces shared traffic dramatically but regresses end-to-end cost.
Wake-driven waiting does not outperform polling.
Root-level order diversification violates the current move-witness contract.
More widely spread recursive order offsets increase total CPU/cycles.
Persistent shared cache greatly increases reuse but regresses repeated-solve economics.
Simple shifted shared-slot decorrelation is workload-dependent and regresses a hard probe.
Shared writer contention is negligible at current mask 7.
Lower direct-map replacement is not sufficient to predict lower runtime.
